EXCLUSIVE: The untold story of the FBI’s J6 pipe bomber “Person of Interest #2”
If what the
@FBI

’s January 6 pipe bomber “Person of Interest #2” (POI2) told me about his FBI interview is true, there is further proof that the Bureau has covered up, or “deleted,” additional video footage about what happened when the RNC pipe bomb was allegedly discovered by Karlin Younger on January 6, 2021.  I will not reveal the identity or any other identifying information about the FBI’s POI2 in the January 6 pipe bomb saga. I also won't discuss the full five hours of personal interview time with POI2; instead, I will focus on two key pieces of information he gave me.  As a primer for those not already following this story in detail, here is a brief rundown of the facts in POI2’s case and why the FBI was initially interested in him as a “person of interest”:  -POI2 does not live in the Greater D.C. area. He lives in a large American city in a state that does not border D.C.  -From news releases, congressional reports, FBI statements, and an FBI whistleblower disclosure, we know that POI2 was visiting a lifelong acquaintance (POI3) at his residence in Fall Church, VA, over the course of January 4 - 7, 2021.  -POI2 used POI3’s Metrorail card for travel back and forth to the District on the 5th and 6th.  -POI2 caught the attention of law enforcement investigators when he emerged from D.C.’s Metro South rail station on January 5, changed hats and put on dark sunglasses, then beelined straight across the street from the station into the Rumsey Court alley behind the Republican National Committee headquarters. It was in that alley that POI2 began taking photos of “numbers.” Numbers on trash cans, dumpsters, door addresses, and the like. According to the FBI, POI2 planned to use those photographs in a forthcoming book. (To date, that book has not been published.) Then, after walking around Capitol Hill all day long, and even attending some of the J5 protest events, POI2 ducked back into the same alley for a few minutes — after dark — before returning to the Metro South station across the street from the RNC. He returned to Falls Church via the train, where POI3 picked him up by car, and they went back to POI3’s home. POI2 then returned to DC the next morning to attend Trump’s speech at The Ellipse on the 6th.  -POI2 was cleared of suspicion following two FBI interviews on January 19, 2021, at his residence in his home city. These interviews took place six days after the FBI pulled their Special Operations Group (SOG) surveillance team off POI3’s home on January 13, just two days after they were deployed to watch the infamous Falls Church, VA condominium address where we now know POI3 shared a firewall between his address and the then residence of former Capitol Police officer Shauni Kerkhoff. The subject of our November 8, 2025 story published by Blaze Media.  How I came to spend five hours with POI2 I met with POI2 twice, on December 11 and 12, 2025. On the 11th, a member of our team accompanied me: a retired FBI veteran of 25 years now working as a private investigator. That first interview lasted for three hours, and then the next day I met with POI2, just him and me, for another two hours.  I arrived in POI2’s home city on the 10th to do some early recon. We had POI2’s name (which I’d acquired from a congressional source), and his address, but we didn’t have a current phone number. After running an extensive background on him, we learned a lot about his life and work, social media, friends and close associates, and even where he attends church, but we still didn't have a phone number to call him and ask for a meeting.  Most interesting of all, POI2 is a prolific international traveler. In one recent year, he had logged over 40 international flights. So we didn’t even know if he’d be in the country, much less at home, if we knocked on this door.  My recon of his address was a huge disappointment. His apartment building is one of those old inner-city manufacturing plants refitted into modern, upscale housing. The entire property is ringed by tall wrought-iron fencing, with electronic security for entry into the parking garage, foot traffic, and into the building itself. There was no visible way for us to just pay him a visit for a “knock and talk.” Perhaps we could have “buzzed” him from an exterior gate, but I didn’t get that far that day.  Later that evening, I picked up my team member from the airport — the retired FBI guy — and we went to dinner for a long, late-night planning session. We identified a couple of strong local personal connections he had via his Facebook page, and we planned to visit them first, get more info about POI2, and maybe even get their help reaching out to him.  At 9:00 a.m. the next morning, we arrived at the home of someone who seemed like they might be closest to him. We were lucky and hit a home run on the first swing. Without the long details, our “story” about why we were looking for POI2 — their close friend — worked like a charm, and we were invited into their home. Our host called POI2, and within two hours POI2 joined us at our new friend’s home. Luckily, POI2 had returned to the States from an overseas trip only the day before.  For the next three hours, I asked most of the questions while my partner listened and observed. Based on my partner’s 25+ years of experience with the FBI, he believed POI2 answered everything truthfully … “Or, he’s a very, very good liar.” My partner had to fly back home the next morning, but I had many follow-up questions for POI2. I reached out again early in the morning, and he agreed to meet me at a coffee shop in his neighborhood.  ***(On a personal timeline aside: during my second interview with POI2, I was only nine days away from my heart failure episode, and was already struggling to breath after the slightest of physical exertions.)*** The most significant reveal We met at 1:30 p.m., and spent another two full hours together. During this session, we had a detailed conversation about his two interviews with two FBI special agents. Both of those interviews were on the same day. January 19, 2021.  POI2 had explained to the FBI agents that the reason he returned to the Rumsey Court alley behind the RNC was that he remembered there were several trash cans in the alley, and he wanted to dispose of an empty plastic water bottle before going back to the train station.  I asked him why he didn’t simply throw the bottle away at the Metrotrain station. He shrugged. From our video review, POI2 only stayed in the alley for about three to four minutes. But if what he revealed to me is true, it is one of the most significant discoveries in our years-long pipe bomb investigation.  POI2 shared with me that the FBI agents told him that he had thrown the empty water bottle away in the very trash container next to where the bomb would be placed a little over an hour and a half later.  Why that is significant FIRST, it reveals that the FBI most likely had video of him depositing that empty bottle into that container. Yes … they could have taken DNA samples of every item in that trash can, but then they would also have needed DNA from POI2 in their database. POI2 didn’t offer that option as their explanation. He assumed they saw him on camera.  I can personally attest that there is currently a camera in Rumsey Court that would cover the area where the bomb was placed, but I do not know if that same camera existed in January of 2021. But if they did observe POI2, on camera, tossing the bottle in the trash can immediately next to where the bomb was placed, then the FBI most certainly has video of Karlin Younger — the FirstNet employee — who discovered that device at approximately 12:35 p.m. the next day, January 6. Only 25 minutes before Vice President Mike Pence was to drop the gavel on the joint session of Congress to certify the 2020 Electoral College presidential vote. Only about 18 minutes before the first breach of that outer bike rack barricade on the west Capitol grounds, led by Ray Epps, Ryan Samsel, and other suspicious characters.  Many investigators, including Congressman Loudermilk and his committee, have posited that the two devices placed by the gray hooded bomber on J5 were retrieved at some point in the early morning hours of J6, then replaced just before their “discovery” a few minutes either side of 1:00 p.m.  The allegedly “deleted” video from the two DNC cameras that provided the footage of the gray hooded bomber placing a device on the evening of J5 would have also shown us what happened after midnight. Whether or not the two plainclothes Capitol Police counter-surveillance officers were the ones who replaced the device just before reporting its discovery to the Secret Service agents attending VP-Elect Kamala Harris’s presence inside the building at the time. (Article to that story linked in comments below.)  A camera aimed at the RNC drop location would give us the same information about what happened during the night, and when Karlin Younger discovered that device while walking back and forth and doing her laundry. The FBI claims that the footage from the two DNC cameras — after that device was planted under a bench — was accidentally deleted. (No one buys that story.)   Those two FBI agents may also have inadvertently revealed to POI2 that video footage exists from that dark corner of the RNC/Capitol Hill Club alley on J5 and J6.  Both missing videos, if they were to surface, would either invalidate all conspiracy theories about the pipe bombs, or confirm the prevailing theories and circumstantial evidence pointing to law enforcement participation and a multi-agency conspiracy. SECOND, if the two FBI agents were telling POI2 the truth about that specific trash container, then it brings into question all of POI2’s own statements about why he returned to that alley after dark.  That very trash can was in the furthest and darkest corner of the RNC/Capitol Hill Club side of Rumsey Court. He would have had to ignore several of the first and most clearly visible, well-lit trash bins upon his arrival into that alley by way of the walkway between the RNC and the Capitol Hill Club. Instead, he made a hard left behind the Capitol Hill Club and headed toward the darkest corner of the alley, from which the view of that trash can was also likely obstructed by one or more cars typically parked between him and what would be his line of sight to that dark corner.  This implies POI2 was either on a recon mission to determine the best drop location for the second device, or, as one retired, formerly high-ranking law enforcement officer has theorized, he may have placed an AirTag or other electronic beacon to lead the bomber to the most advantageous location to deposit the bomb.  Near the end of my second meeting with POI2, he shared with me several photos of “numbers” he took in that alley. He shared the “time and location” data from those original photos on his iPhone. He also gave me screenshots from his phone’s call history of the exact moment the two FBI agents phoned him for both interviews on January 19, 2021. He was very earnest, forthcoming, and eager to answer all my questions. (Photo examples in comments below.)  As a person, I like POI2. We could be friends. But either he or the FBI is lying about what happened in that dark corner behind the Capitol Hill Club. (Maybe both?)  Just as POI2 and I were about to say goodbye and shake hands, I opened my phone to show him one photo. It was the shot I took of the two side-by-side doors at the condo complex in Falls Church, VA. The door on the left was the home of his lifelong acquaintance, POI3. The door on the right was Shauni Kerkhoff's January 6 residence.  I asked him:  “Can you make this math work for me?” He replied:  “No, man. That’s so weird.” We have stayed in contact and spoken many times since those two days in December. ⬇️

by: KrisAnne Hall, JD

There is a faulty premise at the center of the debate over eliminating homestead property taxes:

“If we eliminate property taxes on people’s homes, local governments will go bankrupt.”

Before accepting the conclusion, perhaps we should examine the premise.

First, homestead property taxes are only one portion of the property-tax base. Eliminating taxes on owner-occupied homes does not eliminate commercial property taxes, taxes on investment property, or every other source of local revenue. Nor does eliminating homestead property taxes mean eliminating local taxation altogether. But there is a much more important point being missed.

Government revenue is not the only measure of a prosperous community.

For generations Americans have lived under a system in which we call ourselves homeowners while knowing that no matter how many years we work, no matter how faithfully we pay the mortgage, and even after the bank’s lien is finally gone, government can still take the home if we fail to make the government’s annual payment. That is not full ownership.

James Madison understood property very differently. In his 1792 essay Property, Madison defined property as the “dominion which one man claims and exercises over the external things of the world, in exclusion of every other individual.” He then identified the very purpose of government:

“Government is instituted to protect property of every sort.” James Madison

And Madison supplied the standard by which government should be measured: a just government “impartially secures to every man, whatever is his own.” Notice the principle: Government exists to secure your dominion over what is yours, not to maintain a perpetual financial claim upon it. That distinction was not academic to America’s Founders. It was at the heart of the controversy that produced the American Revolution.

Samuel Adams warned in 1768:

“For if our Trade may be taxed, why not our Lands?” Samuel Adams

He continued the progression: why not the produce of our lands and ultimately “everything we possess or make use of?” His conclusion was not merely that such taxation was expensive. It was that taxation imposed without legitimate political authority reduced free people to the condition of “tributary Slaves.” That is the Liberty First principle we have forgotten:

Property is not merely an economic asset. Property is an element of liberty itself.

This is why the familiar objection, “If you eliminate homestead property taxes, they’ll just raise some other tax” also misses the point.

Perhaps another tax will rise. That is a separate political battle, and citizens should demand that government justify every dollar it takes and every dollar it spends. But not all taxes burden liberty in the same way. A sales tax may increase the price of something I choose to purchase. A transaction tax may attach to something I choose to do. But a recurring tax on my home places the continued possession of something I already own upon my ability to make another payment to government. Fail to pay a sales tax and government does not take your house. Fail to pay the property tax, and ultimately it can. That difference matters.

The economic discussion also routinely ignores the enormous social value created when people actually own their homes. Imagine communities filled with families whose homes, once paid for, actually belong to them. Retirees would not face an ever-increasing government bill merely for remaining in the houses they spent their lives acquiring. Families would possess an asset capable of creating genuine generational wealth. Economic downturns would not automatically threaten the roof over a family’s head because government still demands its annual tribute. Homeowners would have greater security, greater equity, and greater incentive to improve and preserve the communities in which they have a permanent stake.

We have lived without that kind of ownership for so long that we have forgotten what it means. The question, therefore, should not be framed merely as:

How will local government replace the revenue?

The more fundamental question is:

What would happen to our communities if millions of Americans were finally permitted to own their homes completely?

For generations we have calculated the revenue government receives from taxing the family home while rarely calculating the wealth, security, independence, and liberty the people lose because of it.

Madison told us what property meant: dominion. Samuel Adams warned us where the contrary principle leads: if government may continually tax our trade, our land, its produce, and ultimately everything we possess, what exactly remains beyond government’s claim? A free society should be looking for ways to restore property to the people, not inventing reasons government cannot survive without a perpetual claim upon their homes.

The purpose of government is to secure property. It should not require us to perpetually purchase from government the privilege of keeping what is already ours.

The real purpose of the illegitimate government today is to steal generational wealth, extract the fruits of everyone’s labors, strip away all property rights, and enforce various democide schemes.

It is high time for We the People aka the tax slaves to finally become educated and offer total noncompliance for all forms of social engineering, not limited to the communistic property tax con.

Do NOT comply.

text:
Fun Things to Do in New York for the Rest of 2026

New York City is always buzzing with energy, and the remainder of 2026 offers countless opportunities for travelers looking to experience world-class attractions, entertainment, culture, and unforgettable memories. Whether you're visiting for a weekend getaway or an extended vacation, the Big Apple has something for everyone.

Explore New York's Iconic Landmarks

No trip to New York is complete without seeing some of the city's most famous attractions. Visitors can marvel at the Statue of Liberty, enjoy breathtaking views from the Empire State Building, stroll through Central Park, or visit Times Square's dazzling lights and entertainment. These landmarks provide the perfect introduction to one of the world's most exciting destinations.

Experience Broadway and Live Entertainment

Broadway remains one of New York City's top attractions. From award-winning musicals to family-friendly performances, there is always an exciting show taking center stage. In addition to Broadway, visitors can enjoy live music, comedy clubs, and special events happening throughout the city during the remainder of 2026.

Discover New York's Diverse Food Scene

New York is a food lover's paradise. Travelers can sample authentic New York-style pizza, enjoy fine dining experiences, explore international cuisines, or visit famous food markets like Chelsea Market and Smorgasburg. Every neighborhood offers unique culinary experiences waiting to be discovered.

Visit Museums and Cultural Attractions

The city's museums are among the best in the world. The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Museum of Modern Art (MoMA), American Museum of Natural History, and many other cultural institutions offer fascinating exhibits for visitors of all ages. Art lovers, history enthusiasts, and curious travelers will find plenty to explore.

Enjoy Outdoor Adventures

New York offers numerous outdoor activities, especially during the fall season. Walk across the Brooklyn Bridge, visit the High Line, take a harbor cruise, bike through Central Park, or enjoy scenic views from one of the city's observation decks. US homebuyers are walking away from deals at the highest rate in years:

14.0% of home-purchase agreements that went under contract fell through in July, the highest rate since November 2023.

The national cancellation rate has held between 13.0% and 14.0% over the last 4 years, well above the lower rates typical of the seller's market from 2020 to 2022.

Atlanta posted the highest cancellation rate last month, at 19.8%, followed by Houston at 19.6%, San Antonio at 18.7%, and Las Vegas at 18.6%.

This comes as sellers outnumber buyers by ~51%, near the highest percentage on record, giving buyers more options and making them more willing to walk away over inspection issues, low appraisals, or rejected concessions.

At the same time, high home prices and elevated mortgage rates are leaving buyers with less financial room, making unexpected costs or concerns about taking on large monthly payments more likely to derail deals.

The housing market is under historic pressure.

text:
AMERICA HAS THE OIL. 
SO WHY IS GASOLINE STILL SO EXPENSIVE?

BY DARRELL PITTS

SIMPLE ANSWER: DEMOCRATS.

Americans looking at four-dollar gasoline are being handed an easy explanation BY DEMOCRATS: 
Donald Trump is president, 
therefore these are Trump's gas prices.

The numbers tell a much different  story. 

Go back to March 2022 under Joe Biden. Regular gasoline was roughly $4.32 a gallon while West Texas Intermediate crude was roughly $100 to $113 a barrel. 

Now compare that with late July and much of August 2026. 
Americans were again paying roughly $4.00 to $4.10 for gasoline even while WTI spent much of that period roughly between $79 and $89 a barrel.

That is a remarkable difference. Crude could be roughly $20 or more per barrel cheaper while the gasoline purchased by the American family was only a few dimes cheaper.

Where did the difference go between oil price and gasoline price?

Look between the oil well and the gas pump and you will find refineries.

The Energy Information Administration reported September 4 that since May the New York Harbor gasoline crack spread—the difference between the value of gasoline and the crude oil from which it is made—has averaged approximately $1 per gallon higher than in 2025. 
EIA says both crude prices and unusually high refining margins are contributing to today's gasoline prices.

That means blaming the todays pump price on Trump—or on insufficient American oil production—doesn't explain what is happening.

America has oil.

The bottleneck increasingly involves refineries that turn that oil into finished fuel.

The United States remains an extraordinary energy producer. EIA expects American crude production to average approximately 13.8 million barrels per day in 2026. American refineries were recently operating at an extraordinary 98 percent utilization rate, the highest since 2018.

In other words, America's remaining refineries aren't simply sitting idle.

They are running extremely hard.

Yet finished gasoline remains tight.

That is where decades of decisions about refining capacity become important.

America's refinery system is heavily concentrated along the Gulf Coast. 

The East and West BLUE Coasts, controlled by Democrats,  are much more dependent upon gasoline manufactured somewhere else. 

EIA specifically says those two blue/Dem. coastal markets rely on imports to supplement domestic production.

That creates one of the strangest contradictions in American energy policy: 

the world's leading crude-oil producer can simultaneously import finished gasoline into major coastal markets because of Democrat policies.

California provides the clearest example of how this happened.

California requires its own cleaner-burning gasoline formulation, which EIA says requires additional processing and expensive blending components. 

Its Cap-and-Invest program and Low Carbon Fuel Standard add additional costs. 
California is also geographically isolated from America's enormous Gulf Coast refining system.

Then California began losing refineries.

-Marathon ended conventional petroleum refining at Martinez. 
-Phillips 66 converted Rodeo away from conventional crude refining. 
-Phillips 66 closed its Los Angeles refinery. 
-Valero ceased refining at Benicia.

The Los Angeles and Benicia closures alone represented approximately 17 percent of California's refining capacity.

Meanwhile, Californians didn't stop driving.

California's own Energy Commission has acknowledged the basic problem: 
the state's refining capacity has been shrinking, leaving, legislated out of exsstance faster than its demand for petroleum fuel.   
The demand is still there but the supply is gone due to Democrat regulatory policies.

That means leftist Democrats must import fuel.

EIA reached the obvious conclusion. 
Because California cannot readily replace lost refinery output through pipelines from Texas and Louisiana, the likely replacement for much of the missing gasoline and jet fuel increasingly comes from Asia.

Think about the absurdity.

America possesses enormous petroleum resources. An American state discourages petroleum investment while its citizens continue consuming gasoline. 
Domestic refinery capacity disappears. 

The need or gasoline stays. 
It is increasingly manufactured elsewhere and transported across an ocean.

That isn't energy independence.   It is relocation of industrial capacity.  
It is energy production dependence on foreign countries that are America's enemies.

The East Coast arrived at a related vulnerability through a similar path. 
It has lost considerable refinery capacity over the years and consequently relies heavily upon Gulf Coast pipeline shipments plus foreign imports. 

The enormous Philadelphia Energy Solutions refinery, the largest refinery on the east coast, closed following an explosion and bankruptcy; with no state government help to rebuild or continue as a national necessity.

After the explosion, Democratic Pennsylvania Gov. Tom Wolf's administration specifically said Pennsylvania would not provide new tax support to restart PES. 

 Part of the Green Alliance: Environmental organizations were campaigning for permanent closure.

On the other side were refinery workers, unions, the restart investors and the Trump administration.

But the economic consequence of losing capacity remains the same: the refinery disappears while millions of automobiles remain.

On the other hand, leftist Josh Shapiro offered Eli Lilly 100 million on January 30, 2026 to build its first Pennsylvania manufacturing facility in Fogelsville, Lehigh County, where it plans to manufacture next-generation injectable weight-loss medicines.

Democrat leftist priorities intentionally leave someone else to manufacture the gasoline.

This is where the political philosophy behind American energy policy deserves scrutiny.

The traditional “Red-Green Alliance” referred to cooperation between socialist or social-democratic politics—the Red—and environmental politics—the Green. 

In contemporary political commentary the phrase is also sometimes used for alliances between parts of the radical left and Islamist political activists. 

I use New Red/Green Alliance here as a political description of overlapping progressive movements, not as the name of a centrally controlled organization.

Its participants do not all believe the same things. 

GREEN: LEFTIST Environmental organizations want aggressive decarbonization. 

RED: Democratic socialists want substantially greater government direction of economic life. 
Progressive foundations finance environmental, social-justice and political advocacy. 

GREEN:  Some Muslim-progressive organizations cooperate with the broader left on immigration, civil-rights, energy, foreign-policy and social-justice issues.

They can arrive at the same political demonstration or legislative coalition through completely different doors.

And substantial money exists behind progressive and environmental advocacy. 

George Soros's Open Society Foundations, financed principally by Soros's fortune, announced a $400 million, eight-year initiative supporting what OSF itself calls “green industrial policies.” 

Soros is not accurately described as a conventional Marxist—he made his fortune through capitalism—but his philanthropy has financed a broad range of progressive causes.

It does demonstrate that aggressive progressive economic and environmental transformation has powerful, well-financed institutional advocates.

The important question is what happens when those policies succeed.

If America restricts or discourages petroleum infrastructure faster than Americans stop needing petroleum, the economic activity doesn't vanish.

Someone else gets the business.

And different foreign powers can benefit for entirely different reasons.

China is the most interesting example. 

China doesn't generally benefit from expensive crude because it imports enormous quantities of oil. 

But China has built massive refining, petrochemical, battery, solar and mineral-processing industries. 

If Western industrial capacity contracts while Western consumption continues, Chinese and other Asian industrial capacity becomes more valuable. 

California importing replacement fuel from Asia after losing domestic refinery capacity illustrates the danger perfectly.

Russia's interest is different. 
Moscow depends heavily upon petroleum revenues.

 Higher petroleum prices can increase the value of barrels Russia manages to sell, although sanctions and discounts reduce that benefit.

Iran similarly depends upon petroleum exports and wants maximum value from the oil it successfully sells despite sanctions and current disruptions.

Saudi Arabia is not an American enemy in the same category as Iran, Russia or China; 
it is simultaneously an important U.S. security partner and a major petroleum exporter. 

But its economic interests are not identical to America's. 
Saudi Arabia benefits from sufficiently strong petroleum revenues and has an obvious commercial interest in a world where foreign customers continue requiring petroleum.

Turkey  appears in other Red-Green political discussions. Its relevance would have to be established through a specific energy, financing or political connection.

Beijing, Moscow, Tehran and Riyadh do not need to sit around the same table plotting California environmental regulations.

They pursue their own interests.

The strategic mistake occurs when America voluntarily creates conditions that make foreign industrial or petroleum capacity more important to Americans.

And the current refining market is demonstrating exactly how valuable capacity becomes when supply gets tight.

EIA says global refined-product supplies have been constrained by reduced Russian product exports, disruptions involving the Strait of Hormuz and reduced Chinese refinery runs. 
Those conditions helped push American refinery margins sharply upward. 
EIA expects high crack spreads to keep American refineries running hard through the remainder of 2026.

This brings us back to that Biden-Trump comparison.

When Americans paid approximately $4.32 under Biden in March 2022, crude was roughly $100 to $113.

When Americans paid roughly $4.00 to $4.10 in late July and August 2026, WTI was frequently around $79 to $89.

That does not mean crude prices don't matter.

It means refineries have become a choke point.

And policies adopted years before the current president took office matter.

The retired couple living on a fixed income cares.

And because energy is embedded in transportation, agriculture and manufacturing, expensive energy eventually enters the price of almost everything Americans buy.

There is a human cost of artificially constrained supply. 

We need abundance and competition.

America should make it possible to produce oil, transport it, modernize and expand economically viable refining capacity, protect legitimate environmental interests under predictable rules, and allow competitors to enter when refinery margins become extraordinarily profitable.

If profits become enormous, a healthy free market sends a signal: build more capacity and compete those margins down.

Blue State Governments have created a regulatory environment in which the market receives that signal but investors conclude that building the capacity would be economically irrational.

America has been blessed with extraordinary natural resources, capital, technology and human talent. It should not deliberately turn those blessings into dependence.

The United States should be able to produce American crude, refine American fuel, employ American workers and sell the surplus to allies.

That reduces foreign leverage.

It strengthens American families.

It strengthens American industry.

And it puts competition—not politically managed scarcity—between the consumer and a higher gasoline price.

America did not run out of oil.

The warning flashing at the pump is that oil in the ground is not enough.

A nation must preserve the pipelines, refineries, ports, storage and industrial capacity required to turn its resources into useful energy.

That is the difference between possessing energy and possessing energy independence.

text:
🚨India's data centre boom gathers steam as US expansion faces resistance

Across the US, more than 15 states have proposed curbs on data centre development over concerns about power demand, water use, and impacts on communities.

 New York has paused new large-scale projects for a year, while Texas is halting new grid connections as it reviews energy-use plans.

In June, voters in Monterey Park, California, permanently banned data centres, the first US city to do so. 

For India, these developments offer an early warning.

“India has an opportunity to learn from the US. The lesson is not to slow data centre development, but to assess the economic, social and environmental trade-offs upfront," said Ashish Banerjee, Senior Principal Analyst at Gartner. "Power and water availability, ratepayer protection, noise, local benefits and community acceptance should become part of site selection and approval.”

India's data-centre capacity crossed 2.1 GW at the end of the June quarter, according to data from S&P Global and CBRE. Around 200 MW was added in the first six months of the year, and an additional 500 MW is expected to be added through the rest of 2026. 

Amazon, Microsoft and Google have committed nearly $57 billion in less than a year towards AI, cloud and data-centre infrastructure in India.

The opportunity is considerable. India generates nearly 20 percent of the world's data but hosts only about 3 percent of global data-centre capacity. 

But building enough infrastructure to close that gap will require more than just capital.

It will require electricity, land, connectivity and increasingly, access to resources that are already under pressure in some parts of the country. The question is whether India can build the data-centre infrastructure required for its AI ambitions without running into the power, resource and community conflicts now emerging in the US

text:
To comprehend why numerous home purchases are falling through today, it’s essential to reflect on the tumultuous buying frenzy from 2020 to 2022. Throughout the pandemic, historically low mortgage rates sparked an unprecedented rush to buy homes. Intense bidding wars erupted, with multiple offers pouring in within hours of listings being posted. In that frantic atmosphere, sellers had the upper hand; buyers frequently waived standard protections like home inspections and appraisals, offered more than the asking price, and overlooked property flaws to secure shelter. Contract cancellations were uncommon because backing out meant losing the sole opportunity to purchase a home.  

Now, fast forward to the present, and that frenzy has dissipated under immense financial strain. The Federal Reserve raised interest rates to curb inflation, pushing mortgage rates into the 6% to 7% range. Meanwhile, home prices did not experience a major decline; they remained near record highs. This combination has led to the most severe housing affordability crisis in a generation. For today’s homebuyer, obtaining a new mortgage now requires a substantial portion of monthly income, draining household savings and leaving little financial buffer for unexpected costs.  

This financial vulnerability is clashing with a significant shift in market dynamics. With high borrowing costs, overall buyer interest has cooled, while new builds and existing homes have gradually entered the market, resulting in sellers outnumbering active buyers by more than 50%. Buyers now have more flexibility and choices. When they enter a contract and discover a $12,000 roof leak during the inspection, find an HVAC system nearing the end of its life, or face an appraisal that deems the house overpriced, buyers are no longer willing to overlook these issues. They insist on price reductions, repair credits, or concessions from the seller.  

The impasse reaches a tipping point right at the closing table. Many sellers remain emotionally tied to the booming years, expecting top dollar and unwilling to reduce prices or cover repairs. However, current buyers, wary of taking on an unaffordable monthly payment for a compromised property, know they have the advantage. Instead of conceding, they utilize their inspection or financing contingencies, retrieve their earnest money, and exit the deal, particularly in oversaturated markets like Atlanta and Houston, where another property is just down the street.

text:
According to Trump “You  might not love his look, you might not love his television interviews or how he dresses, but Ken Paxton was the best AG ever 

The Best Little Résumé in Texas
Trump and Ken Paxton want Texans to send him to the U.S. Senate, and he’s asking them to do it with a rap sheet a normal candidate would need a law firm just to summarize on a bumper sticker.
Start with the securities fraud indictment — three felony counts, filed within months of him taking office as attorney general in 2015. The case dragged through the courts for nearly nine years before prosecutors let him settle it in 2024 for 100 hours of community service and, by other accounts, nearly $300,000 in restitution. Nine years is long enough to raise a child from birth to fourth grade. Paxton spent it as the state’s chief law enforcement officer while under felony indictment for the exact kind of financial misconduct his office is supposed to prosecute.
Then there’s the impeachment — not a partisan smear from Democrats, but a bipartisan 121–23 vote by the Republican-controlled Texas House in May 2023, on charges of bribery, abuse of office, and obstruction of justice, all tied to his relationship with a donor under federal investigation. The Texas Senate acquitted him on all 16 articles that September, along party lines — not exactly a resounding declaration of innocence so much as a coin flip that landed on his side of the aisle. The Justice Department later quietly declined to pursue its own bribery investigation into the same conduct, in the final days of an outgoing administration — the kind of timing that resolves a legal problem without ever resolving the underlying question.
Add a taxpayer-funded settlement — $3.3 million — paid to the whistleblowers he fired for reporting him in the first place. That’s not a legal fee. That’s Texans footing the bill for their attorney general’s retaliation.
None of this stopped him. He’s won every election he’s run since the fraud indictment first landed, including his first reelection as AG while under indictment, and last spring’s primary against a sitting U.S. senator. That’s not a loophole in the system. That’s the system working exactly as his campaign has learned to exploit it: flood the timeline with grievance, outlast the news cycle, and let “acquitted” do the work that “innocent” can’t.
The pitch now is simple — trade a scandal-plagued attorney general for a scandal-plagued senator, and hope the upgrade in title distracts from the downgrade in accountability. Texas has never elected a Democrat statewide since 1994, and Paxton is counting on that streak more than he’s counting on his record. Whether that’s a safe bet is the only real question on the ballot. Whether it’s a good one is a separate matter entirely. The question is will Texans give Paxton greater opportunities to commit crimes that the U.S. senate has to offer.

text:
Small business owners built the American Dream. Democrats want to take it from you | Fox News

Imagine living the American Dream, taking a risk to build a business from nothing, only to watch your tax dollars subsidize the government-backed competitor across the street.

That is exactly what is happening in New York, where a coalition of small business owners went to court last week to stop the Mamdani regime from using taxpayer dollars to compete directly against them.

That is socialism on Main Street. That is the Democratic Party's economic agenda.

Small businesses are not merely one sector of the American economy. They are the American economy. There are roughly 36 million small businesses across the country, employing nearly half of America’s private-sector workforce.

For more than 50 years, my family has operated a car dealership in Weatherford, Texas. In all that time, I have never been the sole dealer in my market, nor have I asked the government to make me one. In our business, we compete for our customers, and they, not the government, decide who wins.

That is capitalism.

Socialism takes that choice away. It does not build a better store. The government picks up the tab, leaving the small business owner across the street to compete against an opponent whose losses are someone else’s problem.

Republicans chose a different path.

Through the Working Families Tax Cuts, we made the 20% small business deduction permanent, giving Main Street businesses the certainty to invest, expand and hire. On average, 8 million small business owners are keeping an extra $4,600 — helping them breathe a little easier.

Full expensing, for example, allows a machine shop to deduct the entire cost of qualifying new equipment in the year it's purchased. We also ended the tax on tips and overtime pay so hardworking Americans can keep more of what they earn.

Already, nearly 20 million workers have benefited from overtime relief alone. We cut red tape, saving $211.8 billion in regulatory costs last fiscal year. In May, the SBA doubled the maximum loan size available to growing businesses, from $5 million to $10 million. The result is an economy where entrepreneurs are once again willing to bet on themselves. Small business optimism is running above its 52-year average, hiring plans are the strongest they have been since 2022, and in July alone, Americans filed 578,926 applications to start new businesses.

That is what happens when Republican leadership puts Main Street first.

Democrats call their approach compassion. Look at what happens to the people they claim to help.

Los Angeles is phasing in a $30 hourly wage for hospitality workers, and a survey of owners this spring found that roughly 650 jobs had already been lost. New York's delivery-pay mandate allegedly shrank the ranks of active delivery workers by nearly 28,000 and increased the fee on every order by 72%.

Fewer jobs, higher prices, and small businesses are left holding the bill.

Republican-led states have taken a different approach. Over the past year, my home state of Texas added 165,600 jobs — more than any other state. Dallas Mayor Eric Johnson, who left the Democratic Party in 2023, now calls his city "America's Sanctuary City from Socialism."

Same country, same economy, different parties in charge. The results speak for themselves.

As chairman of the House Committee on Small Business, I will always fight for the people willing to put their own money and time on the line to build something of their own. Government should create conditions that enable entrepreneurs to succeed, not use taxpayer dollars to compete against them.

Every single Democrat in Congress voted against the Working Families Tax Cuts. They voted against permanent tax relief for 36 million small business owners. They voted against Main Street.

The choice could not be clearer.

Socialism offers you a government store. Capitalism offers you the keys to your own.

The business owners in that New York courtroom are not asking for a handout. They are asking for something far more fundamental: the freedom to compete, the room to build something of their own, and the right to keep what they have worked so hard to create.

•~INR 1,000 cr capex a year for the next 3 years
•Preform, fibre and cable capacity to rise 50% against visible demand
•New greenfield Optical Connectivity Facility in India for high-density / AI / DC assemblies
•R&D spend ~2% of average annual revenue
•10+ advanced plants across India, North America and Europe
•~9% of global optical-fibre market outside China; 785+ patents
•Full stack in-house: glass → fibre → cable → connectivity solutions

Business Development
•Moving from component supplier to co-development of the customer’s connectivity architecture
•Integrated offer: fibre + cable + assemblies + connectors + systems to take more of the stack
•In development: hollow-core fibre, multi-core fibre, 13,000-fibre-count cable
•Co-packaged optics and near-packaged optics started in-house as optics move to the chip
•Four Lakshya drivers: larger optical TAM, customer co-development, integrated solutions, tech differentiation

Strategy 
•Telecom remains a base load; AI data-centre and DCI are the incremental, less-cyclical engines
•Aim is to become one of the largest global digital-connectivity players by FY29
•India end-to-end manufacturing used as speed and proximity advantage for hyperscaler India capex
•Balance sheet described as now able to fund the Lakshya capex without a separate capital raise on the call

Balance Sheet
•No new net-debt or WC-days number on this meet
•CFO: strengthening balance sheet is what funds the INR 1,000 cr annual capacity and downstream spend
•A risks-and-assumptions slide was shown but not read out on the call

Other Key Updates
•Speakers: Ankit Agarwal (MD), Ajay Jhanjhari (Group CFO), Rahul Darak (IR)
•Meet was a strategy/Lakshya launch, not a full Q1 P&L walkthrough — Q1 figures stay at “highest-ever revenue and EBITDA”

text:
In 2022, LIV Golf burst onto the professional golf scene like an activist investor storming into a sleepy company: an effectively unlimited checkbook, stars acquired at eye-watering prices, a disruptive format, team play, 54 holes, no cut. A genuine shock to a golf establishment still comfortable with its old habits and assumptions.

The PGA Tour immediately understood the threat. LIV wasn't simply launching another competition; it was trying to buy the market. And it did what any massively capitalized new entrant does when it wants to gain market share fast: break the market price to capture the market.

Rahm, Koepka, Johnson, DeChambeau, Mickelson... were lured by guaranteed contracts, some reportedly worth nine figures. Sporting performance almost became secondary to asset acquisition. The player was a balance-sheet item: a brand to capture, an audience to monetize, an asset whose future value was supposed to justify today's burn.

In financial terms: massive cash burn, no clear path to profitability, and a valuation thesis built on future market dominance.

Except a golfer isn't a tech company. You can buy a player; it is much harder to buy the audience, media rights, sponsors, the majors, world ranking points and, above all, a century of golf history. LIV had acquired prestigious assets. It still had to build the ecosystem capable of turning them into sustainable revenue.

The PGA Tour fought back with suspensions, sanctions, litigation and pressure on players. Then came the surreal moment of June 2023: the PGA Tour, DP World Tour and PIF announced a framework agreement to bring the pieces back together. The war was supposed to become a merger. Instead, it became an interminable negotiation.

Meanwhile, LIV kept burning cash. The PIF could finance a model no traditional sports organization could realistically sustain. But even a sovereign wealth fund eventually looks at return on invested capital and asks whether the capital deployed is generating anything remotely resembling an acceptable return.

In 2026, the faucet gets turned off. The financial miracle suddenly looks less like a golf revolution and more like an emergency restructuring. LIV is cutting headcount, canceling events, seeking roughly $250M to $350M in fresh capital and reportedly considering Chapter 11. Some players have reportedly even been offered settlements worth pennies on the dollar against guaranteed sums.

That is perhaps the most delicious part. For years, LIV told the golf world that the old model was obsolete and doomed. Today, it is LIV's own business model that needs life support.

And the biggest paradox may be yet to come: one of LIV's most valuable assets may no longer be its players, teams or tournaments, but its tax losses. Roughly $5B in accumulated operating losses could attract BC Partners, reportedly considering a deal around $300M.

The financial predator sees what the golfer doesn't: sometimes a business worth little as an operating company can be worth considerably more as a tax asset wrapped in a distressed corporate structure.

The LIV that set out to revolutionize professional golf could therefore end up as a case study in distressed investing and restructuring.

And the players are learning an old lesson of capitalism: a guaranteed contract is only as good as the counterparty's ability to honor it.

Some may look back toward the PGA Tour. Others will renegotiate. The most powerful may try to turn contractual claims into equity in whatever LIV 2.0 eventually emerges.

Meanwhile, the PGA Tour could end up welcoming back some of the prodigal sons it once pushed away.

The ultimate irony? LIV was designed to break the PGA Tour's dominance.

It may ultimately help reinforce it.

Because in finance, just as in golf, taking a massive risk isn't necessarily the hard part.

The hard part is figuring out who is going to pay the green fee when the bill finally comes due.

#LIVGolf #PGATour #Golf #SportsBusiness #Finance #PrivateEquity

text:
The biggest lie in interview prep: "If I just solve more LeetCode problems, I'll get a FAANG offer." 

I've seen engineers solve 500+ problems and still get rejected.

I've seen others solve half as many and land life-changing offers.

One engineer solved 600+ LeetCode problems over 14 months.

Another solved 250 carefully selected problems in 7 months.

Guess who got the better offer?

This is the uncomfortable truth about prepping for FAANG and top tech companies:

More preparation does not automatically lead to better results.

More often, it leads to:
- Resource hopping
- Random job applications
- Watching system design instead of practicing it
- Ignoring OS, DBMS, and networking
- Finishing 30% of every roadmap and 100% of none
- Collecting notes instead of building skills

The candidates who stand out usually do something different:
- Master core DSA patterns
- Practice real system design interviews
- Build a solid foundation in computer science fundamentals
- Understand AI and modern software engineering trends
- Build projects that demonstrate depth
- Spend time interviewing, not just studying

The biggest lesson I learned:
Top companies don't hire the candidate who solved the most problems.

They hire the candidate who can solve problems they've never seen before.

That's why fundamentals beat memorization.

text:
🟨 *Rachana Bhog* for the Mother is prepared in the Math itself, preparations begin from the day of Mahalaya. About two thousand coconut narus are made for the Mother along with muri and other arrangements. All kinds of seasonal fruits are offered to the Mother as Naivedya, along with cashews, raisins, dates, amsatta. There is a tradition of sacrificing sugarcane, ash gourd and banana in front of the Mother. It is necessary to mention here that there are separate arrangements of Naivedya for the puja of all Gods, Goddesses, their vehicles and Anga deities, after offering each Naivedya, the place is cleaned and another Naivedya is brought.

🟩 At night, the Mother's bhog includes luchi, cholar dal and moong dal, three kinds of curries and five kinds of fries and sweets, kheer, rabri. At night there is no non-veg item in the Mother's bhog, everyone's bhog is vegetarian. During the offering of bhog at noon and night, an asana is spread in front of the plate and Tulsi is given on Narayana's bhog and Bel leaves are given on the bhog of Mother Durga and everyone else. At exactly 12 noon, bhog is offered followed by Bhogarati and at night bhog is offered after 8 pm. The morning Balya Bhog is offered within the time of the forenoon puja. On Ashtami day, if the tithi ends before twelve o'clock, bhog is offered once within Ashtami itself and then again the usual midday bhog is offered along with arati.

🟥 *Dashami Bhog*
On Dashami day, as Visarjan Kritya bhog in front of the Mother, Dadikarma bhog is offered which mainly contains flattened rice and curd, raisins, cashews, various fruits, banana, naru, sandesh etc.

🟨 Every day in the Math, Khichuri bhog is distributed in the name of the Mother. In the bhog cooking room itself, this bhog is offered in front of the Mother's picture and arati is done, then it is served on the plates of visiting devotees as the Mother's Mahaprasad. This khichuri is prepared with rice, dal and all kinds of vegetables, there is no separate labra or anything like that, along with it there is chutney and the boundless blessings of Mother Annapurna. Regarding the khichuri bhog of the Math, we find in a letter of Swami Virajananda, one-time President of Belur Math - 'Only khichuri will be arranged in sufficient quantity. Whatever vegetables etc. you give in it. No other curry or sweets are needed. This khichuri will have to be offered as a huge bhog in handa after handa in front of the Mother and then served to the Sarvahhara Narayanas. This time Mother will accept puja-bhog in this way and our puja will be successful. No separate arrangement for anyone.'

🟠 As Thakur Sri Ramakrishna says, 'Mother eats through a hundred mouths'. To put this thought into action, every branch of Ramakrishna Math across India makes distinct arrangements for the Mother's bhog, and they also give special importance to ensuring that her children also get Mother's compassionate Prasad on Puja days. And by the grace of the Mother, no one returns unfed from any branch of the Math and Mission.

text:
This is not written by me, I don't know who wrote it either, but from old experience I can say it is very relevant and acceptable in today's situation. How we will celebrate Durga Puja was decided by our former sages, what we will eat will also follow the path directed by them, it is better for the self-proclaimed Babas or Gurujis of two days not to interfere.
♦️ *Bhog of Mother Durga at Belur Math* ♦️
The main large plate of non-veg bhog is for the Mother and the rest are for Lakshmi, Saraswati, Kartik, Ganesh, Nabapatrika, Maha Singha and Mahishasura. In Belur Math's independent Lakshmi and Saraswati Puja, non-veg is not offered, but at this time since they are present as companions of the Mother, non-veg bhog is a must.
On Saptami, Ashtami and Navami morning, after the main puja of the Mother, i.e., the Shodashopachara puja, Balya Bhog is offered. This Balya Bhog consists of a big brass pot of khichuri and whole Hilsa fish fried with spices. This bhog is offered only for the Mother, not for any other Gods or Goddesses.
🟥 *Midday Bhog*
Now coming to the items of the Mother's midday bhog. White rice for the Mother is of Gobindobhog rice and the pulao offered to the Mother is made with Basmati rice. These rices are sorted and cleaned from the day of Mahalaya by the young Brahmacharis of the Math, so that no pebble is found in the Mother's bhog. On the plate of Anna Bhog, white rice is given in a heap, beside it in bowls are given khichuri and pulao along with payesh, i.e., paramanna. On the Mother's plate there are five kinds of boiled items like boiled raw banana, potato, pointed gourd, pumpkin and bitter gourd. Among fries, the Mother's bhog includes fried potato, pointed gourd, brinjal, bitter gourd and bori. For the Mother, Goyna Bori is brought from Medinipur. All kinds of seasonal and off-season vegetables available in the market are used to prepare curries and dalna for the Mother. From cabbage, cauliflower to jackfruit, banana blossom, everything is there in the Mother's vegetable curries. All kinds of curries are beautifully arranged in separate bowls for the Mother. Along with it, fries and boiled items are beautifully arranged beside the plate. Earlier, the Mother's bhog was offered in earthen vessels during Durga Puja, but according to senior monks, these earthen vessels would pile up after offering bhog, so large bell-metal plates and bowls were arranged for the Mother. A few people are always ready just to wash these utensils. With everything on the Mother's bhog plate, salt, lemon and separate glasses of water are also given.
Since the Mother's bhog is offered with non-veg, there is a special arrangement for fish items. At least five kinds of fish are given every day, if more fish is available than that, then that too is given. Among the five special kinds of fish, every day there is Hilsa, Prawn, Rohu, Bhetki and Sarpunti.
🟧 *Sandhi Puja*
In Sandhi Puja, the Mother is given a large bhog, which includes all kinds of Anna bhog, curries, fruits, sweets and various fish preparations along with the sacrificial meat from Kalighat. As per the instructions of Sri Sri Mother, animal sacrifice is not done at Belur Math, the sacrificial goat is offered to the Mother at Kalighat on the days of Durga Puja Sandhi Puja, Shyama Puja and Phalaharini Puja and that Prasad meat is brought to the Math, cooked and offered as bhog. When a Prasad offered to one Goddess is again offered as bhog in the puja of another Goddess, then it becomes Mahaprasad. Just like in Puri, Jagannath Dev's prasad becomes Mahaprasad after being offered to Mother Bimala.

text:
India’s kombucha brands are using familiar flavours to make the category approachable, while at the same time experimenting just as much with more unusual flavour combinations.

I mapped the most recurring flavours across the brands in my kombucha research.

Mango was the most common, offered by 8 brands, followed by Peach at 7.

Pineapple, Blueberry and Ginger appeared across 6 brands each, while Strawberry showed up across 5.

But the interesting part is what happens beyond the familiar fruit flavours.

Brands are also experimenting with Hibiscus, Rose, Apple Cinnamon, Ginger Lemongrass and Apple Spice.

And a lot of the most interesting flavours do not appear on this chart because only one brand is offering them.

I found examples like Basil Shikanji, Beet Pomegranate, Blue Spirulina & Ginger, Cacao Orange, Chilli Guava, Coffee Vanilla, Cuban Watermelon Mojito, Earl Grey Lavender, Elderflower Muskmelon, Gor Keri, Indie Chaat, Koshimbir, Lemon Mint & Basil, Mango & Chilli, Mango Coconut, Naga Pepper, Peach Vanilla, Pineapple & Basil, Pomegranate Rose, Rasam, Rice & Pandan, Spiced Jamun and Blueberry Rose.

That mix tells me the category is still exploring what consumers actually want from kombucha.

Some flavours make the drink feel more familiar and easier to try. Others help brands lean into kombucha’s fermented, botanical and craft identity.

And when you look at flavour cues across combinations, ginger and lemon appear again and again, which makes sense given how naturally they fit with acidity and fermentation.

The flavour playbook in Indian kombucha is still being written.

I’ve also put together a free dataset of the kombucha SKUs I mapped across India. Link in the comments/replies

The full deep dive will be published soon. Follow for updates.

text:
Angolan food and agriculture magnate Nelson Carrinho is set to end three decades of Portuguese ownership at Banco de Fomento Angola through his group's financial arm. Congolian Financial, the Lobito-based vehicle beneficially owned by Carrinho and his brother Rui Alves Candundo Carrinho, has agreed to buy Banco BPI's entire 33.35% stake for $452 million, or 388.5 million euros. The deal covers 5,002,500 shares and was announced by BPI on Sept. 3. Nelson Carrinho is president of Grupo Carrinho and Rui Carrinho is vice-president. The price is structured in three parts: $401 million payable on completion, $51 million due in May 2027, and a variable amount equal to half of BFA's 2026 dividend attributable to the shares, also payable in May 2027. BPI, a subsidiary of Spain's CaixaBank, carried the holding at $441 million at end-June and expects the fixed payments to add about $10 million to shareholders' equity.

Completion remains subject to several conditions. The National Bank of Angola must raise no objections, the Capital Market Commission must confirm Congolian Financial does not need to launch a mandatory takeover offer, and Unitel, BFA's largest shareholder, must waive its pre-emption right. The exit has been long in the making. BPI once held 48.1% of BFA and has been trying to reduce Angolan exposure since 2017 under European Central Bank pressure, with a 2023 sale attempt halted by kwanza depreciation. For Grupo Carrinho, the move builds on a broader push beyond its core in flour, pasta, rice and cooking oil into finance. The group entered banking in 2021 with Banco de Comércio e Indústria and has pursued control of Banco Keve. Congolian Financial also acquired 7.61% of BFA around the bank's 2025 listing before transferring it to the AXIOS fund, a step reports linked to avoiding a concentration scenario.

text:
The Crown's Promise, Not the Colonies': Emancipation and the American Revolution

During the American Revolution, the promise of freedom in exchange for military service against Great Britain did not come from the thirteen colonies or their revolutionary governments — it came from the British Crown. A popular but historically inaccurate narrative holds that the rebelling colonies, particularly in the South, offered enslaved African Americans their freedom if they took up arms against the British. The historical record shows the opposite: it was British officials, beginning with Lord Dunmore's Proclamation of 1775 and expanded by the Philipsburg Proclamation of 1779, who offered emancipation to enslaved people who fled their patriot masters and joined the royal cause. When southern patriots did entertain the idea of freeing enslaved men for military service, as in John Laurens's proposal to the Continental Congress, their own state legislatures rejected it outright. The southern colonies-turned-states did not grant freedom to slaves for Revolutionary War service; the practice and the policy belonged to Britain.

The clearest evidence of British initiative is Lord Dunmore's Proclamation, issued on November 7, 1775, by John Murray, the royal governor of Virginia. Dunmore declared martial law and promised freedom to "all indented servants, negroes, or others" belonging to rebel masters who were willing and able to bear arms for the Crown. Between eight hundred and two thousand enslaved men answered the call, forming what became known as Lord Dunmore's Ethiopian Regiment, whose members reportedly wore sashes reading "Liberty to Slaves." Four years later, British commander Sir Henry Clinton extended this policy through the Philipsburg Proclamation of June 30, 1779, which promised freedom to any enslaved person in rebel-held territory, regardless of whether they took up arms. Historians estimate that tens of thousands of enslaved African Americans — some put the figure as high as one hundred thousand — sought refuge with British forces over the course of the war as a direct consequence of these two proclamations. This was a policy of the British Empire, not of the colonies rebelling against it.

Southern patriot governments, by contrast, treated the arming and emancipation of enslaved people as a threat rather than a strategy. The most direct test case is the effort of John Laurens, a South Carolina officer and aide to George Washington, who proposed in 1778 that the Continental Congress authorize the recruitment of enslaved men into Continental Army regiments, with freedom granted upon completion of service. Congress approved the concept in March 1779, but only on the condition that the state legislatures of South Carolina and Georgia consent to it. Both refused. Laurens brought the proposal before the South Carolina House of Representatives in 1779, again in 1780, and a final time in 1782, and it was defeated decisively every time, opposed by figures such as Governor John Rutledge and Christopher Gadsden. No regiment was ever raised, and no slave in South Carolina or Georgia was freed under the plan, because the plan never became law. The southern states had the opportunity to adopt an emancipation-for-service policy of their own and declined it repeatedly.

The contrast between British action and southern inaction reveals why the two are so often, and so mistakenly, conflated. Because both the British and figures within the Continental cause floated the idea of freeing enslaved soldiers, popular memory has sometimes collapsed the distinction between a proposal that was debated and rejected by American state governments and a policy that Britain actually implemented on a mass scale. Enslaved people themselves understood the difference at the time: it was toward British lines, not toward Continental Army recruiters, that tens of thousands fled seeking liberty. The historian Cassandra Pybus and others have described this movement as one of the largest self-emancipations in American history prior to the Civil War, and it happened because of British, not American, promises. The southern states' rejection of the Laurens plan was not an aberration but consistent with their broader unwillingness to disturb the institution of slavery even under wartime pressure.

In sum, the historical evidence does not support the claim that the thirteen colonies, or the southern colonies specifically, offered freedom to enslaved people who fought in the Revolutionary War. That offer came from the British Crown through Dunmore's and Clinton's proclamations, and it was British forces, not American ones, who received the enslaved people who acted on it. When a comparable proposal was raised within the American camp, southern legislatures rejected it more than once rather than enact it. Any account that credits the revolutionary colonies with offering slaves their freedom in exchange for service inverts the actual historical roles of the two belligerents in this particular chapter of the war.

Bibliography

Egerton, Douglas R. Death or Liberty: African Americans and Revolutionary America. New York: Oxford University Press, 2009.

Frey, Sylvia R. Water from the Rock: Black Resistance in a Revolutionary Age. Princeton: Princeton University Press, 1991.

Gilbert, Alan. Black Patriots and Loyalists: Fighting for Emancipation in the War for Independence. Chicago: University of Chicago Press, 2012.

Holton, Woody. Forced Founders: Indians, Debtors, Slaves, and the Making of the American Revolution in Virginia. Chapel Hill: University of North Carolina Press, 1999.

Holton, Woody. Liberty Is Sweet: The Hidden History of the American Revolution. New York: Simon and Schuster, 2021.

Jasanoff, Maya. Liberty's Exiles: American Loyalists in the Revolutionary World. New York: Alfred A. Knopf, 2011.

Lawler, Andrew. A Perfect Frenzy: A Royal Governor, His Black Allies, and the Crisis That Spurred the American Revolution. New York: Atlantic Monthly Press, 2023.

Massey, Gregory D. John Laurens and the American Revolution. Columbia: University of South Carolina Press, 2000.

Pybus, Cassandra. Epic Journeys of Freedom: Runaway Slaves of the American Revolution and Their Global Quest for Liberty. Boston: Beacon Press, 2006.

Quarles, Benjamin. The Negro in the American Revolution. Chapel Hill: University of North Carolina Press, 1961.

Schama, Simon. Rough Crossings: Britain, the Slaves, and the American Revolution. New York: Ecco, 2006.

text:
India's first listed company treating children no one talks about. 
#MomsBeliefIPO #RaysOfBeliefLimited

IPO Review : Rays of Belief Limited (Mom's Belief)

This company helps children with Autism, ADHD, Down Syndrome, Cerebral Palsy, and Learning Disabilities.

These are called Neurodevelopmental Disorders (NDDs).

And this is India's largest For Profit Social Enterprise in this space.

They provide therapy, early intervention, parental guidance, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and family support programs.

Target age group? 
Children aged 18 months to 12 years. 
For older kids up to 15 years, they offer vocational and life skills training.

How big is this network?

136 centres. 
57 cities. 
20 states and union territories.

They operate through owned centres, partner led centres, school collaborations, and even online therapy.

They also have a Centre of Excellence and an Upskilling Academy.

Now let's talk numbers.

Revenue jumped 124% in one year. 
From ₹36.4 Crore in FY25 to ₹81.6 Crore in FY26 (consolidated).

Profit Before Tax grew from just ₹0.35 Crore to ₹6.9 Crore.

PAT in FY26 was ₹4.96 Crore. 
It looks lower than FY25's ₹5.88 Crore. 
But FY25 had a one time deferred tax credit. 
So actual growth is strong.

EBITDA margins are improving fast. 
FY24: 4.87% 
FY25: 8.28% 
FY26: 14.59%

Now the IPO details.

Price Band: ₹227 to ₹239 per share. 
Face Value: ₹10. 
Issue Size: ₹125 Crore. 
100% Fresh Issue. 
No OFS. 
Lot Size: 62 shares.

IPO opened on 1st September. 
Closed on 3rd September. 
Listing date is today, 8th September.

P/E ratio at upper band? 74.45x. 
And there are zero listed peers in India to compare.

This makes valuation tricky.

Where will the ₹125 Crore go?

₹41.36 Crore for setting up 319 new centres across India. 
₹14.45 Crore for lease payments of existing Indian centres. 
₹10.13 Crore for US centre lease and license payments. ₹10.21 Crore for brand awareness and outreach programs. 
Remaining for acquisitions and general corporate purposes.

Yes, they are in the US too.

They acquired Mom's Belief US Inc. and a Virginia based allergy clinic. 
US operations alone contributed 41.74% of consolidated revenue in FY26.

That is ₹34 Crore from the US business.
Now the promoter.

Nitin Bindlish. Chartered Accountant. 19 years in healthcare. 
He was named Social Entrepreneur of the Year 2023. Also featured in BW BusinessWorld's 40 Under 40 list.

Corporate promoter is Carving Futures Pte. Ltd. from Singapore. 
They hold 91.43% of the company before IPO.

The company has 340+ full time clinical professionals. Employee costs are 52.48% of total expenses. 
This business runs on skilled people.

Revenue comes from 3 segments. 
32% from Indian centre operations. 
25.56% from export services to the holding company. 41.74% from US centres.

Now some important things you must know.

Early pre IPO investors got shares at ₹112 per share. That is a 53% discount to the IPO price.
But recent investors in 2026 paid ₹284 to ₹290. 
That is 19 to 21% above the IPO price.

Rainmatter Investments (Zerodha's fund) is also an investor.

Anchor investors include Viney Growth Fund, LRSD Securities, Nova Global Opportunities Fund, and others.

Now the red flags. Read these carefully.

🔴 Cash flow from operations is negative at ₹1.94 Crore. Cash flow from investing is also negative at ₹6.18 Crore. This is a concern. The company is not generating free cash.

🔴 25.56% of revenue comes from related party transactions. 
That is from Carving Futures, their own holding company. 
If this agreement ends, revenue takes a big hit.

🔴 All centres run on leased premises. 
Lease tenures are just 11 months to 3 years. 
And 30 to 37% of capex goes into fit outs that can't be moved. 
If a lease is not renewed, that money is gone.

🔴 The company has delayed statutory payments in the past. 
ESIC, EPF, GST, TDS delays were reported. 
They now have a compliance framework but this is still a concern.

🔴 Some Key Managerial Personnel could not trace their degree certificates. 
They used mark sheets and affidavits instead. Governance question.

🔴 No listed peer exists in India. 
You cannot benchmark this company against anyone. Valuation is completely based on trust and growth story.

The moat?
Proprietary clinical system. 
Structured therapy protocols. 
Digital tracking tools. 
Parent empowerment modules. 
Asset light model with rapid expansion capability.

The company covers Autism, ADHD, Down Syndrome, Cerebral Palsy, Intellectual Disability, Learning Disabilities, and Global Developmental Delays.

A noble cause with a business model around it. 
But the red flags are real and cannot be ignored.

Not a recommendation. 
Just an educational review. 
Do your own research before investing.

Indira Gandhi turned to Moscow just as South Asia approached war. On August 9, 1971, with armed conflict looking increasingly possible, Indian foreign minister Swaran Singh and Soviet foreign minister Andrei Gromyko signed a twenty-year Treaty of Peace, Friendship and Cooperation in New Delhi. For a country that had made non-alignment central to its foreign policy, the agreement was an extraordinary move.

The decision grew out of a crisis that had begun months earlier in Pakistan. After the Awami League won Pakistan’s 1970 general election, the transfer of power stalled. On March 25, 1971, the Pakistani army launched a violent crackdown in East Pakistan. Fighting spread, the Bengali independence movement hardened, and refugees poured across the border into India. By the end of the year, roughly ten million people had fled into Indian territory. Gandhi’s government regarded that burden as economically and politically intolerable, while also supporting the Bengali resistance. The possibility of an India-Pakistan war was no longer theoretical.

India’s problem was not Pakistan alone. Pakistan was closely aligned with China, which had fought India in 1962. Washington under Richard Nixon was also maintaining its relationship with President Yahya Khan, whose government was serving as a secret channel in the American opening to Beijing. Henry Kissinger visited China secretly through Pakistan in July 1971, and Nixon announced his planned trip to China on July 15. American records show that Indian officials were deeply concerned about the possibility of Chinese intervention if war came. New Delhi increasingly feared that a conflict with Pakistan could become a larger strategic confrontation in which India might face Pakistan while China stood behind it and Washington remained unwilling to support India.

Soviet option had existed before the immediate crisis. Moscow and New Delhi had been discussing a friendship treaty since 1969, but India had resisted anything that looked too much like a formal alignment. By the summer of 1971, that hesitation weakened. The final treaty carefully preserved language of non-alignment: Article IV explicitly stated Soviet respect for India’s non-aligned policy. But Article IX gave the agreement its strategic weight. Each side promised not to assist a third country fighting the other, and if either was attacked or threatened with attack, the two governments would immediately consult on “appropriate effective measures” to remove the threat. It was not an automatic mutual-defense pact, but neither was it an ordinary declaration of friendship.

Washington understood the difference immediately. A State Department memorandum prepared the day the treaty was signed described it as a dramatic demonstration of Indo-Soviet closeness and noted that it offered India the prospect of Soviet support if war came. Henry Kissinger worried that agreement might make India feel freer to act against Pakistan. Yet the treaty did not mean Gandhi had simply joined the Soviet camp. Two days before it was signed, her office accepted an invitation for her to visit Washington, and Indian officials quickly reassured the United States that the pact was not directed against it. Gandhi was narrowing India’s strategic vulnerability, not abandoning every other relationship.

Four months later, value of that calculation became visible. War widened dramatically on December 3 after Pakistan launched air strikes against Indian airfields in the west. Indian forces then fought on both fronts while supporting the Bengali independence struggle in the east. At United Nations, Soviet Union repeatedly used its veto against Security Council resolutions calling for an immediate ceasefire and withdrawal before the military and political outcome in East Pakistan had been settled. That diplomatic protection gave India time. Pakistan’s eastern command surrendered in Dhaka on December 16, and Bangladesh emerged as an independent state.
